A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViStoryBench, with matching datasets, evaluation framework, and generation methods. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, human ratings, metric-human correlations, and reference-image sensitivity results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and human-evaluation results and adds Lite-subset validation and a prompt-alignment comparison in Appendix D.1 and G.5.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Figure 3 expand the reported CIDS feature extractor for realistic characters from ArcFace to ArcFace, AdaFace, and FaceNet. This changes a component of the benchmark's evaluation procedure; the generation-method adaptations and broader benchmark pipeline remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 80 stories, 1,317 shots, 344 characters, 509 reference images, and 20-story Lite subset, with English and Chinese prompts. The added analyses examine retained benchmark coverage; no additional evaluation dataset, language, or task is reported.

E2.justification: v3 adds CLIP-based similarity and VinaBench's GPT scoring as comparators in the prompt-alignment case study (Appendix G.5, Figure S5). The evaluated generation-method roster remains unchanged. DreamBench++ and OmniContext in Table 1 are descriptive benchmark comparisons, not newly evaluated generators.

E3.justification: The reported human-study design changes from three annotators scoring all stories (v1 Appendix H) to 20 annotators with randomized partial assignments and at least ten ratings per model-story pair per dimension (v3 Appendix F). CIDS also uses revised feature extractors. New validation protocols compare full versus Lite results and scoring methods across six example shots. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds two distinct validation analyses: Lite-subset representativeness through category distributions and full/Lite metric comparisons (Table S1, Figure S3), and expert-judged prompt-alignment comparisons against CLIP and VinaBench (Figure S5). These substantially expand benchmark validation. The earlier reference-image-selection analysis is retained as Table S7, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 describes averaging annotator scores. v3 additionally states that standard deviation across annotators is reported, introducing an uncertainty-reporting description. However, Table S5 still supplies means only, without numerical standard deviations. Fixed-seed generation statements remain unchanged, with no new multi-seed uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: CIDS values change throughout the main and Lite tables under the revised evaluator. For example, full-set UNO cross/self CIDS changes from 39.4/67.1 to 44.6/59.9; Lite GPT-4o cross-CIDS changes from 53.2 to 58.9, overtaking AIbrm, which changes from 55.9 to 55.8. These are revised metric results, not demonstrated generation improvements under identical evaluation. v3 also adds Lite-validation results and qualitative scoring-comparator findings; human-rating tables remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal task specification and OCCM equation remain unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical proofs, and the added feature extractors and empirical distribution comparison introduce no new mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: v3's conclusion adds an explicit claim to provide the first large-scale, multidimensional comparison, while its abstract sharpens the distinction from single-image and reference-free benchmarks. The central contribution remains the same diverse story dataset and twelve-metric evaluation suite.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning Lite's reliability as a proxy and the proposed alignment evaluator's advantages over CLIP and VinaBench. Section 4.2 newly identifies missing background-reference and scene-consistency evaluation, plus specialist-model limitations and VLM hallucination risks. Appendix A also adds specific copyright and reuse qualifications alongside the retained limitations.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents manual review of LLM-generated scripts and expands annotation-interface, annotator-training, and workflow information, including an interface screenshot. Most generation adaptations, long-prompt handling, supplied system prompts, hardware information, and evaluation runtimes are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to DreamBench++, OmniGen2/OmniContext, Captain Cinema, AdaFace, and FaceNet. Table 1 and Section 2.2 explicitly contrast ViStoryBench with DreamBench++, OmniContext, and VinaBench. This sharpens benchmark positioning while retaining most earlier related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, metric explanations, conclusion, and several appendix discussions are extensively rewritten. Appendices are reorganized: dataset-construction prompts move from H.1 to B.2, style-similarity details from C to I, and the user study from H to F. The earlier contents listing is removed.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, moves the dataset overview before the abstract, revises captions and table styling, and reformats prompt boxes. It adds benchmark and Lite-comparison tables, category-distribution and polar visualizations, an annotation-interface screenshot, and Figure S5. Existing qualitative examples and calculation diagrams are largely retained but resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: Clearer presentation, explicit limitations, and added validation improve several aspects, but central reporting problems prevent a reliable net judgment. v3 reports UNO-Lite CIDS as 44.6/59.9 in Table 2 and 47.3/61.3 in Table S4, whereas v1's corresponding tables agreed. The substantially revised human-study description also retains identical rating results without displaying its claimed standard deviations. The PDFs do not resolve these inconsistencies sufficiently to establish an overall quality improvement.
